mission-board.lede: Most live threads are in the same state: the making is done, the sending isn't — client work sits approved and undelivered, an offer sits ready without a named buyer, a studio sits built with no pilot run, and the listening engine keeps filing posts the system has no record of anyone publishing. The genuinely new thing this window is a verdict arguing the current lead offer should be parked.
mission-board.next_move: Ship a finished thing to a person outside the system before starting anything new.
mission-board.caveats: Everything here is assembled from what the harness recorded. Sends, posts, calls and client reactions happen off-system, so an empty outcome column means "not logged", not "not done". Several threads also carry titles captured from unrelated finalize notes, and most quality scores are self-assigned rather than judged against real published work.
mission-board.operator_read: Nothing is blocked; almost everything is unsent.

first-client-engine.lede: A zero-based re-derivation of what Farrice should actually sell landed here, and it argues against the current lead offer: park the Angle Map and sell a tightly bounded workflow pilot to small professional-service firms, scoped small enough to finish and measure. It is a verdict, not yet a decision — nothing downstream has been changed to match.
first-client-engine.next_move: Accept or reject this verdict out loud, then make the campaign and offer threads agree with whichever way it goes.
first-client-engine.caveats: The verdict reasons from Farrice's stated capability and cash need, not from buyer evidence — nobody has been asked to pay for the pilot. It also contradicts the live campaign, and both are currently running.
first-client-engine.operator_read: The system just argued against its own active campaign, and that fork needs a human answer before more work compounds on either side.

linkedin.lede: The channel work keeps closing missions — offers wargamed, profile copy rewritten, launch content drafted — but what the ledger shows is preparation, not sends. Nothing in this window was finalized as a shipped deliverable or logged against an outcome.
linkedin.next_move: Send the posts and outreach that already exist instead of opening another round of positioning work.
linkedin.caveats: Activity here is inferred from files written and missions closed; whether anything was actually posted, or drew a reply, happens outside the system, so the empty outcome column may understate real sends.
linkedin.operator_read: LinkedIn is fully armed and hasn't fired — the bottleneck is sending, not making.

angle-map-listening-engine-v4-1.lede: The listening engine genuinely runs: each cycle produces a brief with a flagship post and finished assets filed ready to publish, and it feeds its own living docs without a person restarting it. It is the closest thing here to a machine that converts input into publishable output on its own.
angle-map-listening-engine-v4-1.next_move: Publish what the engine has already filed as ready before running another cycle.
angle-map-listening-engine-v4-1.caveats: Output quality is self-scored and sits in the middle band, and the scheduled job behind this engine has been flagged as falling behind its cadence — so "active" may describe its last good run rather than a current one. A verdict on another thread argues for parking the Angle Map as the lead offer entirely, which would change what this engine is for.
angle-map-listening-engine-v4-1.operator_read: The best-running machine we own is producing posts the system has no record of anyone publishing.

proof-to-market.lede: The offer itself is settled — positioning, price frame, guarantee language and buyer-council pressure tests have all been through a full pass, and the handoff reads ready. What has not happened is putting it in front of a named buyer.
proof-to-market.next_move: Pick a real supplement or performance brand and send the offer to a named person there.
proof-to-market.caveats: Everything backing "ready" is internal: council runs and grounding passes, not a prospect reaction. Demand for this exact offer stays unconfirmed until someone pays. A newer zero-based verdict elsewhere argues Farrice should lead with AI workflow work rather than messaging-led offers, and the two have not been reconciled.
proof-to-market.operator_read: The offer is done being designed; it is now purely a distribution problem.

01-listing-content.lede: The listing package went through repeated rejection and rebuild — hooks reworked after they read as feature announcements, then the bodies rewritten as lived scenes — and landed on an approved recording pack. It is sitting in the clean pack waiting to be handed to the client.
01-listing-content.next_move: Send the approved recording pack to Jen.

why.0: The open item is polish on supporting formats. It does not gate the handoff, and holding the pack for it delays the only thing the client actually needs.

01-listing-content.caveats: "Approved" here means approved internally — there is no record of the client filming, posting, or reacting, so nothing is known about how any of it performs.
01-listing-content.operator_read: Client work that is finished and undelivered — the shortest path to a win on this board.

video-studio-edit-bay.lede: The studio is built and has already generated a substantial pile of assets, but none of the planned pilots has been run end to end. Several pieces are cloned or scaffolded rather than wired, so "ready" describes the build, not a proven run.
video-studio-edit-bay.next_move: Run a pilot start to finish and tell Farrice exactly what voiceover to record.

why.0: Until a pilot runs whole, the untested pieces stay theoretical — and a pipeline that reports ready without ever having run is precisely the failure this system keeps trying to kill.

video-studio-edit-bay.caveats: The unwired components and untested integrations are known and written down rather than discovered; the vertical reframing step is acknowledged as crude, so vertical output should not be assumed usable.
video-studio-edit-bay.operator_read: A studio with no film shot in it yet.

extract-forge.lede: The extraction pipeline is the most productive thing in the system right now — expert after expert has gone through it and come out as a working skill. What remains is not build work; it is Farrice's own blind verdict on whether the output reads as the real expert.
extract-forge.next_move: Decide whether that blind verdict is worth a session — if not, close the thread and keep using the skill as it stands.

why.0: This is a taste verdict, not a defect. Left open, it makes a finished build read as unfinished on every board it appears on.

extract-forge.caveats: The scores this pipeline assigns itself skew low, and self-scoring is the only grade most of these extractions carry — volume is far better evidenced here than quality.
extract-forge.operator_read: The extraction engine works; what's unresolved is whether we trust our own grade on it.

oren-slop-era-creative-strategy.lede: The extraction ran and a blind-pass sample exists, but the output was graded as needing improvement and nothing finished has been filed against the thread since. Recent sessions have drifted toward adjacent creative-strategy questions rather than closing this one.
oren-slop-era-creative-strategy.next_move: Run the blind pass against a real published piece and either promote the skill or record why it failed.
oren-slop-era-creative-strategy.caveats: The grade on this extraction is self-assigned and low. Sessions attached here span more than this skill, so the thread's apparent activity overstates progress on the skill itself.
oren-slop-era-creative-strategy.operator_read: Extracted but unproven — there's been motion near this thread, not on it.

trailer-treatment.lede: A director-level package for an original animated trailer exists — reference pack, continuity rules, and a master prompt built to hold character and world consistency across shots. The ledger shows nothing generated from it.
trailer-treatment.next_move: Generate from the master prompt and judge the resulting shots against the continuity rules.
trailer-treatment.caveats: This is a craft track with no revenue line attached and an outcome row that is still empty; treat it as an experiment rather than a deliverable with a customer waiting.
trailer-treatment.operator_read: The hard part — canon and continuity — is done, and the thread stalls at pressing go.

04-briefs.lede: The brief and readout layer shipped and is now the surface most other threads render into: templates, a board shelf, agent context packs, and a consistent brand skin across all of it. It graded well and has been quietly absorbed into daily use.
04-briefs.next_move: Close this thread and let any further change be driven by a downstream thread that hits a real limit.
04-briefs.caveats: The thread's title was captured from an unrelated build note, so its label understates what it is. The work is verified by build checks, not by evidence that anyone read a brief and acted differently because of it.
04-briefs.operator_read: The readout layer is done and earning its keep; it doesn't need a driver.

system-audit.lede: This thread shipped a change to how the harness defaults to evidence-backed judgment and pushback, plus repairs to the verification and routing telemetry around it. It has been quiet since, and it carries a title picked up from an unrelated client deliverable.
system-audit.next_move: Decide whether the judgment-floor change is settled — close the thread if it is, or name the behavior still misfiring if it isn't.

why.0: It has gone quiet while still marked open, and an audit thread that lingers half-open makes every future audit look unfinished.

system-audit.caveats: The shipped work self-scored below the system's own keep bar and was never re-graded. The mislabeled title also means anyone finding this thread by name will misidentify what it contains.
system-audit.operator_read: The judgment floor landed, the thread never closed, and its name points at the wrong work.
